supported_findings: Saved IDs, labels, normalization and perturbation bounds matched; modified images were used.
Source-model gradient matching produces a locally malicious update; the basic attack mechanism is present.
The matched poisoned victim fits the perturbed training examples with their true labels while retaining the correct target label.
Warm-starting from the actual trained source and disabling translations separately did not rescue this failed case.
Freshly optimizing an attack for the otherwise identical ReLU architecture also failed in this case.
The max defense approximation cannot cause the standard baseline failure because standard training has no defense regularizer.
limits: Detailed interventions concern one preselected failed target (2 to 7), not a new 25-trial study.
These results identify weak end-to-end attack efficacy in this setup; they do not isolate a unique architecture/dataset cause or prove robustness.
CIFAR width-32 pilot had 1/3 successes; it is not the paper width-64 ConvNet or a statistically precise estimate.
The maximum-budget MNIST pilot has two completed failures; its third case and SE stage did not finish.
No new defense comparison has been launched.
